long_biography.plain_text:
Auto-Vehicle Parts placed Homan at the centre of a specialised manufacturing business supplying clips and fasteners to the automotive aftermarket. He became its principal shareholder and owned the company for almost sixty years. After acquiring the historic F.A. Neider operation, he modernised the plant and introduced employee profit sharing, linking expansion with a practical change in workplace benefits.

Homan also developed and renovated prominent Cincinnati properties. His projects included the Vernon Manor Hotel, the River Terrace apartments and the conversion of Madison House into 175 luxury condominiums. Beyond business, he and his wife Margo established the Homan Foundation in 1969. Their giving supported charitable causes and educational access, including endowed assistance at Xavier University and scholarships associated with Cincinnati schools.
